responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for IBM S/390 and z/Architecture (System z), responsible for turning GCC’s generic IR and RTL into correct, tuned code for 31-bit and 64-bit S/390 environments and their OS variants. Its core is the main backend implementation and target headers (`s390.cc`/`s390.c`, `s390.h`, `s390-protos.h`, `s390-modes.def`, `s390.opt`) plus the primary machine descriptions (`s390.md`, `vector.md`, `vx-builtins.md`, `subst.md`, `constraints.md`, `predicates.md`), which together define target options, machine modes, operand legality, instruction patterns, addressing, calling conventions, prologue/epilogue generation, branch/atomic/transactional-memory expansion, vector code generation, and assembly emission. Around that core, the module provides processor-specific scheduling models for many z generations (`2064.md` through `9175.md`) so tuning and instruction ordering match each microarchitecture; frontend integration for S/390 builtins, intrinsics, vector extensions, and target macros (`s390-builtins.*`, `s390-c.*`, `s390-d.*`, `vecintrin.h`, `htm*intrin.h`, `s390intrin.h`); driver support for `-march=native`/`-mtune=native`; and OS or ABI specialization layers such as `linux.h`, `s390x.h`, and the z/TPF files (`tpf.h`, `tpf.md`, `tpf.opt`). Overall, this directory encapsulates the stable System z code-generation, tuning, intrinsic, and platform-adaptation logic that distinguishes the S/390 port from neighboring GCC target backends.
